stem: A team requests compute through a provider API. Which cloud characteristic is demonstrated?

explanations.A: Quotas and capacity limits still apply.
explanations.B: The provider exposes computing capacity when requested.
explanations.C: Using a service does not transfer hardware ownership.
explanations.D: Cloud data can remain private.

stem: What can cloud computing supply alongside compute?

explanations.A: Cloud includes multiple infrastructure capabilities.
explanations.B: Cloud also supplies storage, networking, and managed services.
explanations.C: Cloud supplies compute and storage as well as networking.
explanations.D: Identity is one cloud capability, not the entire offering.

stem: A one-week test needs infrastructure. What cloud capability is useful?

choices.A: Provision resources and release them afterward

explanations.A: On-demand provisioning fits temporary work.
explanations.B: Cloud does not repair all custom code.
explanations.C: That retains hardware beyond the test.
explanations.D: Cloud offerings still impose limits.

stem: Can a fixed-size Azure VM still be a cloud resource?

choices.A: No, every cloud app must scale each minute
choices.C: Yes, autoscaling is a separate configuration
choices.D: Yes, so its capacity is infinite

explanations.A: Automatic scaling is not mandatory.
explanations.B: Cloud also offers compute.
explanations.C: Cloud delivery does not require each workload to autoscale.
explanations.D: A fixed instance has finite capacity.

stem: What changes when server capacity is obtained as a provider service?

choices.A: The team requests capacity instead of procuring that physical server

explanations.A: The provider operates underlying hardware.
explanations.B: Customers still configure workloads.
explanations.C: Service consumption does not transfer facilities.
explanations.D: Cloud delivery does not require public records.

stem: Why does a cloud app still need capacity planning?

choices.A: Quotas and dependencies can limit performance
choices.B: Provider capacity automatically removes every workload bottleneck
choices.C: Every service has identical scaling behavior
choices.D: All cloud capacity is fixed permanently

explanations.A: Provider capacity is not an unlimited workload guarantee.
explanations.B: Dependencies and application design can still constrain performance.
explanations.C: Scaling support and configuration differ among services.
explanations.D: Many services can scale, though limits still matter.

stem: Which action is self-service provisioning?

choices.A: Ordering a rack for next quarter
choices.B: Requesting an allowed resource through an API
choices.C: Waiting for a hardware purchase before every VM request
choices.D: Adding a tag to an existing resource only

explanations.A: That is upfront procurement.
explanations.B: The interface exposes on-demand resource creation.
explanations.C: On-demand cloud APIs avoid this procurement cycle.
explanations.D: Metadata updates do not create new capacity.

stem: What does a managed cloud database provide?

choices.B: Data capability through a managed platform
choices.D: Unrestricted control over the service's underlying operating system

explanations.A: Database access can be restricted.
explanations.B: The customer consumes a defined computing service.
explanations.C: Customers must still design queries.
explanations.D: A managed database abstracts the underlying platform.

stem: Why release temporary resources after testing?

choices.A: Deletion automatically cancels every unrelated subscription
choices.B: Deletion retroactively eliminates all incurred charges
choices.C: Retained services can keep consuming billed capacity
choices.D: Deletion keeps deployed storage permanently free

explanations.A: Deleting lab resources does not cancel unrelated billing scopes.
explanations.B: Already consumed usage may still be billed.
explanations.C: Cleanup prevents unnecessary continued consumption.
explanations.D: Deleting resources ends retention rather than making them free.

stem: Which requirement remains relevant after cloud migration?

choices.A: Direct administration of the provider's physical hosts
choices.C: Requiring every cloud resource to have a public IP

explanations.A: Physical host maintenance belongs to the provider.
explanations.B: Cloud workloads still need reliability design.
explanations.C: Public exposure is not mandatory.
explanations.D: Monitoring remains useful.

stem: A manager says cloud removes every operational duty. What corrects this?

choices.A: All work stays identical to owning hardware
choices.B: The boundary depends on the service
choices.C: Cloud transfers all customer data governance to Microsoft

explanations.A: PaaS and SaaS transfer significant platform duties.
explanations.B: Customers retain work even with managed services.
explanations.C: Customers retain data-governance duties.
explanations.D: Data and identity duties remain.

stem: Which description captures cloud computing?

choices.A: Any remotely accessed server regardless of service capabilities
choices.D: Only event-driven code with no managed databases

explanations.A: Remote access alone does not establish a cloud operating model.
explanations.B: Customers consume services rather than only local hardware.
explanations.C: Buying hardware is not provider usage.
explanations.D: Cloud provides broader services than functions alone.

stem: Who maintains Azure's physical facilities?

explanations.A: Reader access does not operate facilities.
explanations.B: Code ownership does not include provider buildings.
explanations.C: Visitors do not manage infrastructure.
explanations.D: Physical infrastructure is provider responsibility.

stem: Who decides which employees may read customer records?

explanations.A: Authentication alone does not authorize all records.
explanations.B: Physical maintenance does not set permissions.
explanations.C: Hardware manufacture does not decide business access.
explanations.D: Business authorization remains customer-owned.

stem: Who normally patches a typical IaaS VM guest OS?

explanations.A: Provider host maintenance is distinct from guest patching.
explanations.B: Virtual operating systems need updates.
explanations.C: IaaS leaves guest maintenance with the customer.
explanations.D: Connectivity does not maintain guest software.

stem: Which task remains with a PaaS customer deploying custom code?

choices.A: Patching the underlying managed platform OS

explanations.A: PaaS normally handles this layer.
explanations.B: Hardware maintenance is provider work.
explanations.C: PaaS manages the platform, not all customer logic.
explanations.D: Facility operation is provider work.

stem: What remains a SaaS email customer's duty?

explanations.A: The provider maintains the finished application.
explanations.B: Physical hardware is provider-maintained.
explanations.C: That is facility operation.
explanations.D: SaaS retains customer data and identity responsibilities.

stem: An employee leaves. Who should ensure their cloud app access is removed?

explanations.A: Hardware vendors do not manage customer accounts.
explanations.B: Other tenants do not control these identities.
explanations.C: Access lifecycle follows customer personnel decisions.
explanations.D: Power supply does not control business access.

stem: What usually transfers when a VM application moves to suitable PaaS?

explanations.A: Custom logic remains customer-owned.
explanations.B: Customers still classify information.
explanations.C: Customers still decide access.
explanations.D: PaaS increases provider-managed platform responsibility.

stem: Why inspect responsibility guidance for the actual service?

choices.D: The deployment region alone determines every duty

explanations.A: IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS differ.
explanations.B: Service details refine the general model.
explanations.C: Data, code, and identities also need protection.
explanations.D: Responsibility depends on the service and operating boundary.

stem: Who determines the sensitivity of customer files?

explanations.A: A URL does not confer governance authority.
explanations.B: Cooling staff do not set data policy.
explanations.C: Manufacturing does not classify business data.
explanations.D: The organization governs its own information.

stem: Who secures a customer-owned laptop used with SaaS?

explanations.A: SaaS hosting does not transfer endpoint ownership.
explanations.B: It does not maintain every customer device.
explanations.C: Other tenants do not manage this laptop.
explanations.D: Managed hosting does not eliminate endpoint security.

stem: Which IaaS responsibility split is correct?

choices.C: Provider physical hosts; customer guest OS

explanations.A: Visitors do not operate provider infrastructure.
explanations.B: Access and facility duties are reversed.
explanations.C: Infrastructure and guest layers have different owners.
explanations.D: This reverses the normal split.

stem: A managed database engine still requires the customer to do what?

choices.A: Control access and application data use

explanations.A: Engine management does not decide business authorization.
explanations.B: Racks are provider infrastructure.
explanations.C: Managed services supply infrastructure.
explanations.D: Facility systems are provider-managed.

stem: Which risk persists with provider-maintained hardware?

choices.B: Customer failure to repair Azure cooling
choices.C: Customer failure to patrol Azure buildings
choices.D: Customer failure to replace host CPUs

explanations.A: Hardware maintenance does not fix authorization decisions.
explanations.B: Cooling is a provider duty.
explanations.C: Facility access is provider-managed.
explanations.D: Physical hosts are provider-maintained.

stem: How should a SaaS customer protect its information?

choices.A: Configure appropriate access and data handling

explanations.A: Customer governance remains necessary.
explanations.B: SaaS does not justify unrestricted access.
explanations.C: That layer belongs to the provider.
explanations.D: Access should still be reviewed.

stem: A container runs on a customer-managed VM. Who patches the VM OS?

explanations.A: Containers still run on infrastructure.
explanations.B: Visitors do not administer the host.
explanations.C: Containers are not inherently SaaS.
explanations.D: Packaging does not transfer VM host duties.

stem: Who protects Azure physical networking while the customer configures workload rules?

choices.A: Customer cabling; provider all business rules
choices.D: Provider physical network; customer logical controls

explanations.A: This reverses the usual split.
explanations.B: Authentication does not maintain either layer.
explanations.C: Both have security responsibilities.
explanations.D: The physical and workload layers have different owners.

stem: A PaaS app leaks records through a code error. What requires correction?

choices.B: Only Microsoft must rewrite all customer code
choices.D: Only switching to a different billing subscription

explanations.A: PaaS can host flawed customer code.
explanations.B: The customer maintains its custom application logic.
explanations.C: Managed hosting does not guarantee correct custom logic.
explanations.D: Billing scope does not repair a code authorization flaw.

stem: Which review confirms SaaS responsibilities were understood?

choices.A: Confirm the customer must patch the SaaS underlying OS
choices.B: Identify remaining data, identity, and configuration duties
choices.C: Confirm the provider decides every user's business permissions

explanations.A: The provider operates the finished application's platform.
explanations.B: These duties survive the hosting change.
explanations.C: Customers retain business access decisions.
explanations.D: That misunderstands shared responsibility.
